run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T19:31:46Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend request-error alert is explained by two dependencies becoming unreachable from the frontend and checkout: frontend client spans to AdService/GetAds failed with gRPC code 14 UNAVAILABLE / ECONNREFUSED to the ad Service ClusterIP 100.65.180.246:8080, and checkout's PaymentService/Charge client spans failed with code 14 / connection refused to the payment ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080. Both deployments (ad, payment) were replaced at 19:30:12–19:30:16 by a rollout whose pod template was otherwise unchanged (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T19:30:12Z, identical image/env/resources, revision 1→2), and neither deployment defines any readiness/liveness/startup probe, so the new containers were Ready before their gRPC servers accepted traffic. The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, which both deployments consume via FLAGD_HOST=flagd, currently holds the fault-injection settings adFailure="on" ("Fail ad service") and paymentFailure="100%" ("Fail payment service charge requests n%") switched on, naming exactly the two services that were restarted and whose calls failed. I therefore record that ConfigMap as the object holding the enabled fault-injection settings (root_cause), but the conclusion is only partial: the declared application-level fault was not observed (ad and payment emitted zero ERROR spans and no error log lines and kept serving successful requests), the failures seen are transport-level connection refusals coinciding with the rollout, and there is no change history to show who set the flags or when.

claims.text: Frontend span error rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) was exactly 0 from 18:31:46 through 19:31:16, first became non-zero at 19:31:46 (0.337/s), peaked at 3.978/s at 19:35:46 and returned to 0 at 19:42:46; total frontend request-tagged span rate stayed around 40–46/s UNSET through the interval.

Frontend's error spans in the incident are concentrated on GET /api/data (increase 408.27) and its internal/client chain (executing api route (pages) /api/data 408.27, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 408.27) and on POST /api/checkout (45.01, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 45.01, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 45.01), plus tcp.connect 16.07; /api/cart operations recorded 0 errors.

In sampled traces at 19:31:18–19:31:20 the frontend GET /api/data and GET spans carry http.status_code 500 / otel.status_code ERROR, and the child frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carries rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with grpc.error_message "14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080".

In the same sampled traces, checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span ends ERROR with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and otel.status_description "failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = \"transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused\"", and its child span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge carries rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with the same connection-refused description.

Service ad is ClusterIP 100.65.180.246 port 8080/tcp-service with selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, and service payment is ClusterIP 100.70.188.60 port 8080/tcp-service with selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment — the exact addresses that the frontend and checkout errors name.

As of the 19:48 query, endpoints for ad point to pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 (100.96.4.142) and for payment to pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 (100.96.4.221), i.e. the endpoints contained the new pods at query time (a current-state observation, not the incident window).

Cluster events in otel-demo show that at 19:30:12 Deployment ad scaled replica set ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1 and Deployment payment scaled payment-9c8ffb665 from 0 to 1, that pods ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 were scheduled at 19:30:12 and their containers Started at 19:30:14/19:30:15, and that the previous pods ad-554b849958-mbnxm (19:30:15) and payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb (19:30:16) were stopped and their replica sets scaled 1→0.

Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/payment both carry pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T19:30:12Z, are at generation 2 / deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2, and their revision-1 and revision-2 ReplicaSets have identical container image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and ...:2.1.3-payment), identical env (incl. FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013), identical resource limits/requests and identical pod labels — i.e. the rollout restarted the pods without changing the template content.

The ad and payment deployments define only one container each with containerPort 8080 and no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe, so pod readiness is not gated on the gRPC server actually accepting connections.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds demo.flagd.json with the fault-injection flag "adFailure" at defaultVariant "on" (description "Fail ad service") and "paymentFailure" at defaultVariant "100%" (description "Fail payment service charge requests n%"); all other flags read there (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) are off/zero.

The two services whose calls failed are exactly the two named by the enabled settings: frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans show ~0.9–1.4 errors/s from 19:32 through 19:39 and 0 by 19:40, while ad's own server-side oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span rate falls to 0 for 19:33–19:39 and returns (0.75/s) at 19:40; checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client span errors appear at 19:32–19:34 (2-minute rates 0.323, 0.350, 0.022) and are 0 from 19:35.

Error increase by service over 19:30–19:47 shows frontend 1829.2 error spans, frontend-proxy 920.5, checkout 69.7, fraud-detection 2.14 and recommendation 1.07, and 0 for accounting, ad, cart and payment.

Both new pods are current-state Running with all containers ready and restartCount 0, with no lastState termination (no OOMKilled/Evicted/BackOff), and their containers had no previous instance to read.

The new ad pod's retained log lines show it serving normal ad traffic ("Targeted ad request received for [binoculars/books/...]", "Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.") from 19:39:00 onwards, and the new payment pod's retained log lines show "Charge request received." immediately followed by "Transaction complete." from 19:32:15 through 19:39:41 — i.e. successful application-level handling, not failing operations.

Nodes are current-state Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure/NetworkUnavailable all False on all five nodes, including i-0e9f8b08cc290a884 where the new ad and payment pods run (current state only, not incident-time).

Baseline comparison: frontend error-span increase was 0 for 19:00–19:16 and 515.1 for 19:16–19:32; recommendation had 1.03 errors per 16 minutes already before the alert window and 2.06 during it, while fraud-detection moved 0 → 2.06.

The declared fault mode does not match what was observed in the target services: ad and payment recorded zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans of their own and their retained logs contain only successful handling, while the failures exist solely as frontend/checkout client spans failing at transport level (gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE, ECONNREFUSED to the Service ClusterIPs), and the flags adFailure="on" / paymentFailure="100%" are still set while the errors have stopped.

Rejected: that the frontend 500s were caused by the ad and payment services returning application-level errors. The failing spans are the callers' client spans (rpc.grpc.status_code 14, connect ECONNREFUSED) and neither ad nor payment recorded any ERROR span or error log line, so no application-level error response from those services is evidenced.

Rejected: that the recommendation service's flagd EventStream errors or the fraud-detection EventStream errors caused this alert. Recommendation's errors existed before the alert window (1.03 per 16 minutes in 19:00–19:16) and neither service appears in the failing frontend/checkout call paths shown in the error traces.

Primary hypothesis: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is the object holding the fault that produced the frontend error alert. The settings it holds (adFailure="on" = "Fail ad service", paymentFailure="100%" = "Fail payment service charge requests n%") are switched on, name exactly the two workloads that were restarted with an unchanged pod template at 19:30:12 (ad, payment) and the two calls that failed (frontend→AdService/GetAds, checkout→PaymentService/Charge), and no other object was seen applying a fault to those workloads; the rollout restart and the connection-refused errors are treated as its mechanism and consequence.

Alternative hypothesis, left open: the 19:30:12 kubectl rollout restart annotations on ad and payment removed the only ready endpoint of each Service while the new gRPC servers were still starting, and because neither deployment declares a readiness probe the new containers were reported Ready before port 8080 accepted connections, so callers were refused at the ClusterIP (100.65.180.246, 100.70.188.60). This explains the transport-level refusal and the spontaneous recovery without any further object change, but it does not explain why ad's server-side GetAds span rate returned to 0 for 19:33–19:39 after the new pod had briefly served, so it is not adopted as the root cause.

Verify the fault-injection state directly with the flagd UI/OFREP endpoint and audit history for otel-demo/flagd-config (who set adFailure=on and paymentFailure=100%, and when), then set them back off/0 and roll ad and payment again while watching frontend and checkout error rates to confirm whether the flags reproduce the connection refusals.

Add readiness probes for the ad and payment gRPC ports (8080) so that a rollout cannot route traffic to a container whose server is not yet accepting connections, and consider raising the very small CPU limits (ad 50m, payment 20m) that lengthen cold start.

gaps: Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so who or what performed the 19:30:12 rollout restart (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt on ad and payment) and who set adFailure="on" / paymentFailure="100%" in otel-demo/flagd-config, and when, could not be determined.

The declared application-level fault was never observed: ad and payment produced no ERROR spans and no error/exception lines in their retained logs, so the causal step from the enabled flags to the observed ECONNREFUSED refusals is unproven.

Pod readiness and endpoint population over time could not be observed: queries for kube_pod_* and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready returned no data for otel-demo, so whether the ad/payment endpoints were empty during 19:31–19:39 is unknown; endpoints are known only as of the 19:48 snapshot.

Queries for NetworkPolicies and ResourceQuotas in otel-demo returned no objects and no series (only that the query matched nothing), so a policy/quota contribution is neither shown nor excluded; the cluster-wide CronJob query failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.
flagd pod logs for 19:25–19:45 returned no lines, so flag updates, flag evaluation and flagd load around the restart are unverified.
The frontend container returned no retained log lines for 19:30–19:43, so frontend's own application log evidence is missing and the frontend impact is supported only by its spans and metrics.

The ad pod's retained log stream begins at 19:39:00 and payment's at 19:32:15, so container startup output for 19:30:12–19:32 is not available and the length of the post-restart unavailability is inferred from span metrics only.

Caller-side scope beyond the sampled traces is limited: the trace view is a biased sample, so exact counts of failed AdService/GetAds and PaymentService/Charge calls per caller are not established (metric rates above are 2-minute span rates, not request counts).
next_steps: Correlate the 19:30:12 rollout restart and the flagd-config flag values with cluster audit logs/change history to identify the actor and time of both changes.

Set adFailure and paymentFailure to off/0, then observe whether frontend GetAds and checkout Charge errors recur; separately re-apply the same rollout restart with the flags off to see whether the transport-level refusals alone reproduce the alert.
Check flagd (rpc 8013 / OFREP 8016) evaluation logs and ad/payment flag-provider logs for the incident window.
Add readiness probes on port 8080 for ad and payment and review their CPU limits before the next rollout.
